sonnet.problem: Verse 8 has not been told on any story card, so a baker who has only seen the earlier cards can only guess True or False by luck. Card 13's question then repeats the same fact (the singers are waiting for the LORD) as its premise, so the two cards share one point.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

sonnet.problem: The joke laughs at the wicked man, a person in the passage, for not seeing the LORD's majesty. It does not laugh with his human situation.
sonnet.rule: Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

sonnet.problem: The true/false statement tests two claims (other lords ruled over the singers, and they confess the LORD's name alone). It also restates all of verse 13 with no story card before it.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The card tells the dead rising in the dust (death), and a joke comparing the narrator's years in the junk drawer to dwelling in the dust is attached to it.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: Story card 16 quotes "until the wrath has passed," which rules out the wrong answers "gather" and "bless." The blank "punish" is then obvious from the setup.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
